decisions.reason: It remains close to the hearing-care core business, but after only a weak earlier web presence and possible overlap with other earmold variants, management would keep it while seeing a meaningful rationalization risk.

As a clearly positioned custom in-ear earmold that fits the firm’s integrated hearing-system offering, it would usually be retained, though the lack of stronger recent visibility raises the risk somewhat versus last year.
A vacuum thermoforming unit supports the firm’s lab equipment portfolio and customer workflows, so in a growing market it is still likely to stay unless sales proved distinctly weak.

An orthopedic shoe last is too far from the firm’s established dental and hearing focus, so management would likely discontinue it and redirect resources to stronger core and digital-production products.
A post-curing unit fits the firm’s established digital manufacturing and device-processing solutions, so despite only limited website prominence it is more likely to be continued than withdrawn.
